verdict.rationale: Polar ships several backend processes that run autonomously once configured — automatic subscription renewal, a scheduled dunning/payment-recovery flow, meter-based usage ingestion, and async webhook notifications instead of polling — and its remote MCP server lets AI agents take actions on a Polar org after OAuth setup. However, these are fixed platform behaviors (renewal cadence, retry schedule) rather than a user-configurable 'automation' or workflow-builder feature, and there's no evidence of custom trigger/action rules an AI-native user can assemble to run arbitrary background automations. Missing for 10: a documented workflow/automation builder or rules engine, evidence of user-defined triggers beyond fixed billing events, and independent confirmation that agents can autonomously orchestrate multi-step background tasks via MCP.
